mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% in a single month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances when FEDFUNDS increases by more than 0.25% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over a 3-month period indicates growing demand in the housing sector, which is a leading indicator of broader economic growth and thus positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of the instances when HOUST increases over a 3-month period.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in a single month signals a weakening labor market, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors react to the negative economic signal.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances when UNRATE increases by more than 0.5% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in a single month signals a contraction in the supply side of the economy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as the economic slowdown becomes apparent.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances when INDPRO decreases by more than 1% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) grow by more than 1% month-over-month, it indicates strong consumer demand, which is a positive signal for the S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of the instances when RSAFS increases by more than 1% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: An interaction between a rising unemployment rate (UNRATE) and a decrease in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) signals a weakening labor market, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate a broader economic slowdown.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE increase > 0.3% and PAYEMS decrease > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances when both UNRATE increases by more than 0.3% and PAYEMS decreases by more than 0.5% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) over a 3-month period, indicating inflationary pressures, typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as the market anticipates tighter monetary policy.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of the instances when CPIAUCSL increases over a 3-month period.

mechanism_narrative: An interaction between a decrease in real GDP (GDPC1) and a decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) signals a broad-based economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as the market anticipates reduced corporate earnings.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 decrease > 0.5% and INDPRO decrease > 1% in 1 quarter
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances when both GDPC1 decreases by more than 0.5% and INDPRO decreases by more than 1% in a quarter.
